quilting-frame: wooden frame that holds cloth stretched taut for sewing a quilt
cheesecloth: thin loosely woven cotton cloth used for straining or wrapping
tufts: small bunches or clusters of threads, hair, or grass
missionary: person sent to a foreign land to spread their religious faith
elected: chosen by vote for an office or position
grievous: causing great pain, sorrow, or distress
parable: short story that teaches a moral or spiritual lesson
rejoice: feel or show great joy and happiness
physical: relating to the body rather than the mind or spirit
frequent: happening often, or occurring many times over
olden: belonging to old times long past
arise: get up, rise from bed, or come into being
ought: should; is the right or proper thing to do
awfully: very or extremely, in an old-fashioned way
forgettery: made-up word for a place where forgotten things are kept
sakes: used in exclamations like for goodness' sakes, expressing surprise
tick-tock: the steady ticking sound a clock makes
queer: strange, odd, or puzzling in a way that is unusual
pussy: pet name for a cat, used affectionately by children
mamma: old-fashioned word for mother, used by young children
naughty: behaving badly or disobediently, especially in a childish way
spoiled: ruined, or made selfish by giving in to every wish
tears: drops of salty water that fall from the eyes when crying
exclaimed: cried out suddenly in surprise, excitement, or emotion
present: here, in attendance; or a gift given to someone
cents: small coins worth one hundredth of a dollar
jelly: soft, wobbly preserve made from boiled fruit juice and sugar
thread: long thin strand of cotton or silk used for sewing
needle: thin pointed steel tool with an eye for thread, used in sewing
sewing: joining cloth together by stitching with needle and thread
cause: reason why something happens, or to bring about
pleasant: agreeable, enjoyable, and giving a feeling of pleasure
polite: showing good manners and respect toward others
anger: strong feeling of displeasure or rage toward someone
weakness: lack of strength, or a fault or flaw in character
lovely: charming, delightful, or very pleasing to see or hear
generally: usually, in most cases, or as a general rule
birds: feathered, egg-laying animals that fly and sing
tired: weary and in need of rest or sleep
sweetly: in a gentle, pleasant, or kindly manner
gentle: kind, mild, and careful in manner or touch
hummed: sang softly with closed lips, making a low continuous tune
thinks: believes or considers something to be true
slipped: slid out of place or moved quietly away
quiet: making little or no sound; calm and still
outside: in the open air, out of doors, beyond a building
